summary: Port reproduces the Iranian-tricolor layout exactly (identical band boundaries and hue families on the 5x5x5 cloud) but renders it as a bright, near-solid, slowly-churning wash instead of the original's dark, sparse, fast twinkle field with a global ~3.3 s pulse — ~9x mean brightness, ~3x duty cycle, ~5x slower flashes, no pulse, plus an invented amber element in the white stripe.
observations: Both sides have NO controls at all (meta.json controls: [] on orig and port; --probe-controls reports 'no settable controls' for both) — control surfaces match.

Spatial layout is an EXACT match. Classifying each of the 125 cloud pixels by its time-averaged dominant colour gives the identical string on both sides: indices 0-49 red, 50-74 white, 75-124 green (a 2/5 : 1/5 : 2/5 split along the lattice's slow axis, not equal thirds). No off-by-one, no mirroring.

Brightness is ~9x too high on the port. Whole-window meanBrightness over 60 s @5 fps: orig avg 3.7 (min 1, max 7); port avg 32.7 (min 25, max 40). Per-pixel peak channel value is a hard ceiling on each side: orig 40 (median==p90==40 across all 125 px over 120 frames), port 114 — i.e. the port's individual twinkles peak 2.85x brighter.

Duty cycle is ~3x too high on the port, robust to threshold. Fraction of (pixel, frame) samples lit, measured at 10%/25%/50% of each side's own peak: orig 0.247/0.243/0.237; port 0.760/0.703/0.657. At any instant the original lights ~24 of 125 pixels; the port lights ~108 of 125.

Twinkle duration is ~5x too long on the port. Mean contiguous lit-run per pixel (6 s @20 fps, threshold 10% of peak): orig 0.15 s, port 1.07 s (3.1 s at a 25% threshold). Onset rate per pixel: orig ~1.6 flashes/s, port ~0.7/s. The original's near-threshold-independent duty means its blinks are short and sharp; the port's rise/hold/fall is long and smooth.

The original has a strong GLOBAL ~3.33 s brightness cycle that the port lacks entirely. Autocorrelation of meanBrightness shows orig peaks at 33 frames @10 fps, 67 @20 fps, 134 @40 fps — all 3.3 s, so it is time-based and fps-invariant. Port's autocorrelation is a featureless monotone decay with no harmonic series at any rate.

The pulse is visible per-zone, not just in the aggregate: over 6 s the original's per-slab mean brightness swings between 1 and 15 (near-dark to lit, roughly in phase across slabs), while the port's holds 66-88 for the red/white slabs and 37-50 for the green slabs — a ~+/-15% shimmer with no breathing.

The port invents an amber/gold element the original does not have. 3.3% of the port's lit samples are saturated amber (e.g. RGB 109/90/43), all confined to pixel indices 50-74 — the white stripe. The original's white stripe is strictly neutral over 670 lit samples (low-saturation fraction 1.00; full-brightness white is 40/40/46, a faint blue tint).

Hue families match but the green is off. Orig red 40/0/0 (pure), port red 114/2/2 (pure) — match. Orig green at full 0/30/5 (hue ~130, spring green); port green 3/63/36 (hue ~153, sea green). The port's green stripe is also dimmer relative to its red stripe (peak ratio 0.55) than the original's (0.75).

Single steady regime on both sides: a 240 s @5 fps survey shows no mode changes, no palette walk and no drift on either side (brightnessTrend 'steady' on both, first/last means 3/4 orig and 32/35 port).

Both sides are random-driven (seeds 7 and 1234 give different pixel sequences) but statistically stable — the brightness/duty/speed gap above is identical at seed 1, 7 and 1234, so it is not a one-seed fluke.
Neither side is frame-rate coupled: rendering 10/20/40 fps leaves the original's 3.3 s period and both sides' mean brightness unchanged.
feedback: Cut overall output level by roughly 3x: the original's brightest twinkle peaks at max-channel 40/255, the port's at 114/255.

Cut density by roughly 3x: at any instant the original lights ~24 of 125 cloud pixels (24% duty); the port lights ~108 (76%). The original is mostly black with scattered lit points; the port is a nearly solid flag with dark notches.

Speed the twinkles up ~5x: the original's lit runs average 0.15 s (sharp blinks — its duty barely changes between a 10% and 50% threshold, so the on/off edges are fast); the port's average 1.07 s and read as slow crossfades.

Add the missing global pulse: the original breathes with a time-based ~3.33 s period (confirmed fps-invariant at 10/20/40 fps), each zone's mean brightness swinging from near-dark (~1) to lit (~15) and back. The port's zone brightness is essentially constant (66-88 red/white, 37-50 green) with no cycle at any lag.

Remove the amber/gold pixels from the white stripe. The port paints ~3% of its lit samples as saturated amber (e.g. 109/90/43) at cloud indices 50-74; the original's white stripe is strictly neutral white (40/40/46 at full) with zero saturated pixels anywhere in that band.

Nudge the green hue back from sea-green toward spring-green: original full-brightness green is 0/30/5 (hue ~130), port's is 3/63/36 (hue ~153, too much blue). Also raise the green stripe relative to the red one — original green peaks at 0.75x the red peak, port at 0.55x.

Do NOT change the spatial mapping: the band boundaries are already pixel-perfect (indices 0-49 red, 50-74 white, 75-124 green on the default 5x5x5 cloud) and match the original exactly. The control surface (no controls) also matches.
